content:
evan: Quick note - found a race when multiple async requests merge quota headers. Short repro below.

tara: tl;dr?

evan: Run ~100 coroutines hitting chat endpoint concurrently. Responses include quota headers. Our current merge helper does `cache['remaining'] = min(cache['remaining'], header_rem)` which races and can set remaining to 0 or negative.

mike: That explains customer report where clients went into long backoffs.

evan: Proposed fixes: 1) make header parser pure (`parse_quota_headers`) returning ints, 2) stop in-place dict mutations from many tasks: either wrap cache in `asyncio.Lock` or use a single writer consuming diffs from an `asyncio.Queue`. I prefer queue so middlewares stay non-blocking.

tara: Also handle Retry-After variants: sometimes float seconds, sometimes epoch. `parse_retry_after` should convert epoch -> seconds (max(0, epoch - now)). Avoid treating big numbers as seconds directly.

mike: Typing request: expose `AsyncTokenBucket` and `TokenBucket` classes and a small `RateCache` protocol so users can swap in redis-backed stores later. Keep `consume` returning bool and a `wait=True` option for blocking waits.

evan: I opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/pull/1024 (draft) with queue-writer, permissive header parsing, and an examples/async_rate_small.py. CI will run.

rate-bot: PR #1024 queued for CI.

tara: Tests to add: stress test with mixed header formats (int, float, epoch) and assert remaining never negative; mypy check for new public classes.

evan: Will add tests + changelog entry. Workaround in the meantime: set `client.options.rate_merge_mode = 'lock'` or inject a simple `asyncio.Lock` on `client._rate_cache_lock`.

mike: Thanks. This should reduce noisy customer incidents.
